vocabulary.meaning_en: to take milk from a cow; (figurative) to get as much as possible from something
vocabulary.meaning_ar: يحلب؛ يستغل الموقف إلى أقصى حد
vocabulary.example: The farmer milks the cows every morning.
He wanted sympathy, so he told everyone about his cold.

a flat cake with a square pattern, eaten hot
vocabulary.example: We had waffles with honey for breakfast.
Would you like some peas with your rice?

vocabulary.meaning_en: thick cloud near the ground that makes it hard to see
vocabulary.example: The fog was so thick I couldn't see the road.

vocabulary.meaning_en: dirty and harmful substances in air, water or land
vocabulary.example: Air pollution is a problem in big cities.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small amount of food eaten between meals

vocabulary.note_en: Stress CON-tent for the noun; con-TENT (adjective) means happy and satisfied.
vocabulary.example: This website has great content for learners.

to say what is bad about someone or something

to break food with your teeth
approval or kind help; something good you do for someone

fine_lines.title: milk it vs curry favour
fine_lines.explanation_ar: milk it = يستغل موقفاً (مثل مرض بسيط أو إنجاز) إلى أقصى حد لكسب التعاطف أو الاهتمام. curry favour (with someone) = يتملّق شخصاً مهماً كي يحبه أو يمنحه شيئاً.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Milk it' = use a situation as much as possible to get sympathy or attention. 'Curry favour (with someone)' = try to make an important person like you so they will give you something.

examples.sentence: It's only a small cut – stop milking it!
He brings the manager coffee to curry favour with her.

fine_lines.title: roast vs salty
fine_lines.explanation_ar: roast someone = ينتقد شخصاً أو يسخر منه بقسوة (غالباً بمزاح). salty = منزعج أو غاضب بسبب شيء تافه. الأولى فعل تفعله بغيرك، والثانية صفة لحالتك.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Roast someone' = criticise or make fun of someone harshly (often as a joke). 'Salty' = upset about something small. The first is something you do to another person; the second describes how you feel.

examples.sentence: His friends roasted him about his old haircut.
He's still salty about losing the game.

fine_lines.title: waffle on vs something to chew on
fine_lines.explanation_ar: waffle on = يتكلم كثيراً دون قول شيء مفيد. something to chew on = شيء يستحق التفكير فيه قبل اتخاذ قرار.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Waffle on' = talk a lot without saying anything useful. 'Something to chew on' = something to think about carefully before deciding.

examples.sentence: I didn't know the answer, so I waffled on.
Your advice gave me something to chew on.

expressions.meaning_ar: يستغل الموقف إلى أقصى حد لكسب التعاطف أو الاهتمام
expressions.meaning_en: to take full advantage of a situation to get sympathy or attention
expressions.example: He hurt his finger a little, but he's really milking it.

expressions.meaning_en: to choose only the best things or people from a group
expressions.example: You can't cherry-pick the easy questions – answer them all.

expressions.meaning_ar: يتكلم كثيراً دون قول شيء مفيد
expressions.meaning_en: to talk for a long time without saying anything useful
expressions.example: The speaker waffled on for an hour.

expressions.meaning_en: a very thick fog, often with pollution
expressions.example: Our flight was delayed because of a pea-souper.

expressions.meaning_ar: (محتوى) قصير وسهل يمكن مشاهدته أو قراءته بسرعة
expressions.meaning_en: (online content) short and easy to watch or read quickly
expressions.example: I like snackable videos when I'm waiting for the bus.

expressions.meaning_ar: ينتقد شخصاً أو يسخر منه بقسوة (غالباً مزاحاً)
expressions.meaning_en: to criticise or make fun of someone harshly, often as a joke
expressions.example: At the party, his friends roasted him about always being late.

expressions.phrase: (it) leaves a bad taste in your mouth
expressions.meaning_ar: يترك أثراً سيئاً وشعوراً بالضيق بعد تجربة غير لطيفة
expressions.meaning_en: an experience that leaves you with a bad feeling afterwards
expressions.example: The staff were so rude that the visit left a bad taste in my mouth.

expressions.meaning_ar: منزعج أو غاضب بسبب أمر تافه (عامية)
expressions.meaning_en: slang: upset or annoyed about something small
expressions.example: Don't be salty – it's only a game.

expressions.meaning_ar: شيء يستحق التفكير فيه قبل اتخاذ القرار
expressions.meaning_en: something to think about before making a decision
expressions.example: Here's something to chew on: do we really need a new car?
Let me chew on it and tell you tomorrow.

expressions.meaning_ar: يتملّق شخصاً كي يرضى عنه أو يمنحه شيئاً
expressions.meaning_en: to try to make someone like you so they will help you
expressions.example: She offered to do extra work to curry favour with the boss.

grammar.title: Making new adjectives with -able and -y
grammar.explanation_ar: نضيف able- لنقول «يمكن فعله»: snack → snackable (يمكن «تناوله» بسرعة)، wash → washable، read → readable. ونضيف y- لصنع صفة من اسم: salt → salty، cloud → cloudy، taste → tasty.
grammar.explanation_en: Add -able to mean 'can be done': snack → snackable, wash → washable, read → readable. Add -y to make an adjective from a noun: salt → salty, cloud → cloudy, taste → tasty.
examples: a salty answer / a cloudy day
